# SHSAT Cutoff Scores 2026: All 8 NYC Schools + Trends


### TLDR


SHSAT cutoff scores are the lowest composite scores that received offers to each of NYC’s eight testing Specialized High Schools in a given admissions year. For Fall 2026 admissions, cutoffs ranged from 495 at Brooklyn Latin to 561 at Stuyvesant. These numbers are not set before the test, they change every year, and they should be treated as historical benchmarks rather than guarantees. Students preparing for Fall 2027 entry face an additional wrinkle: the SHSAT is now computer-adaptive.


## What Is an SHSAT Cutoff Score?


An SHSAT cutoff score is the lowest composite score that received an offer to a particular testing Specialized High School in a particular admissions year. It is not a passing score, not a predetermined threshold, and not a universal number that applies to all eight schools.


Each school has its own cutoff, created after offers are made.[Greg’s Tutoring](https://www.gregstutoringnyc.com/shsat-cutoffs/) , a well-known NYC SHSAT practitioner, gives one of the clearest explanations of how this works: students are lined up from highest score to lowest, and each student is matched to the highest-ranked school on their preference list that still has an available seat. The score of the last student who fills a seat at a given school becomes that school’s cutoff.


Families often treat cutoff scores as fixed requirements, a line a student must cross to gain admission. That framing is wrong. Cutoffs are outcomes. They result from how many students tested, how they scored, which schools they ranked, and how many seats each school had available. The 2026 Stuyvesant cutoff was 561, but that tells you what happened in 2026. It does not tell you what will happen in 2027.


[Start building test prep habits early](https://miyagilabs.ai/learn) with a guided study path that adapts to each student’s strengths and weaknesses.


## How Is the SHSAT Scored?


The SHSAT uses a composite score for admissions to the eight testing Specialized High Schools. A composite score is the score used to compare applicants during the admissions process. It is not the same as the number of questions answered correctly.


The SHSAT assesses English Language Arts (ELA) and Math. Beginning with the fall 2026 administration, the exam uses a computer-adaptive format, with 50 questions per subject. The difficulty of questions can change in response to a student's answers.


### Is the SHSAT cutoff a raw score or a scaled score?


Families should compare school cutoff scores with the published composite-score scale, not with a simple count of correct answers. The number of questions a student answers correctly does not translate into a guaranteed composite score through a universal percentage formula.


Because the test format and scoring process matter, students should use official SHSAT practice materials and current guidance when assessing their performance. Be cautious with calculators that convert a number of correct answers into a predicted composite score without explaining their assumptions.


### Can you predict your SHSAT score from practice tests?


Practice tests can help identify strengths, weaknesses, pacing problems, and progress over time. However, a practice score is an estimate, not an admissions result. Its usefulness depends on how closely the test matches the current exam format and how accurately its scoring method reflects the official process.


For students preparing for the computer-adaptive SHSAT, use practice resources designed for the new format whenever possible. Track ELA and Math performance separately so that improvements in one subject do not conceal areas needing additional work.

These figures are reproduced across multiple practitioner sites and are described as the[2026 admissions lowest qualifying scores](https://abcmath.com/shsat/cutoff-scores) based on NYC Public Schools data.


A few patterns stand out. Stuyvesant sits alone at 561, well above the rest. The middle schools (HSMSE through Staten Island Tech) cluster between 517 and 539. And the bottom three, HSAS, Brooklyn Tech, and Brooklyn Latin, land between 495 and 507.


Do not read this as a quality ranking. Brooklyn Tech made[1,393 offers in 2026](https://geniusprep.com/specialized-high-schools) , far more than HSMSE (144 offers) or Queens Science (139 offers). A school with more seats can admit students further down the score order, which naturally produces a lower cutoff. That says nothing about the school’s academics, culture, or reputation.

These changes show why a cutoff from one admissions cycle should not be treated as a fixed target. The cutoff is an outcome of the admissions process, influenced by score distributions, school preferences, and available seats. A change in cutoff does not, by itself, establish that a school became academically stronger or weaker.


**How to use the trend:** Compare several years of results where reliable data are available. Pay particular attention to the range of historical scores rather than relying on the most recent number alone.


The practical lesson: never assume this year’s cutoff will match last year’s.


## How SHSAT Cutoffs Are Determined


The eight testing Specialized High Schools use the SHSAT as the[sole admissions factor](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/learning/testing/specialized-high-school-admissions-test) . LaGuardia is the exception; it uses auditions. For the other eight, the matching process is straightforward.


1.


Students take the SHSAT.


2.


They rank the testing Specialized High Schools they want through MySchools.


3.


All students are ordered from highest SHSAT score to lowest.


4.


The system processes each student in turn. It checks their ranked list and offers them the highest-ranked school that still has a seat.


5.


The score of the last student admitted to each school becomes that school’s cutoff.


A concrete example: a student scores 540 and ranks Stuyvesant first, Bronx Science second, Brooklyn Tech third. By the time the system processes this student, Stuyvesant’s seats are full. Bronx Science still has seats. The student gets a Bronx Science offer. They are not penalized for ranking Stuyvesant first.


This brings up the most common and most dangerous misconception about SHSAT cutoff scores.


## Why Ranking Strategy Matters More Than Most Families Realize


Ranking a lower-cutoff school first does not improve your odds of getting into that school. It can only cause you to receive that school’s offer instead of a school you would have preferred.


Practitioners on Reddit report that this question comes up constantly. Students ask whether they should rank Bronx Science above Stuyvesant to “play it safe.” The answer, consistently confirmed by tutors and by the matching mechanism itself, is no. Rank schools in the order you would genuinely want to attend them.


Two rules families should follow.


**Rank by true preference.** If Stuyvesant is the dream school, rank it first. If the student’s score does not reach Stuyvesant’s cutoff, the system will still consider every school ranked below it in order.


**List every school the student would actually attend.** Students can only be matched to schools on their list. One SHSAT community explainer on Reddit highlighted a painful scenario: a student scores above Brooklyn Latin’s cutoff but did not list Brooklyn Latin, and their score falls short of all the schools they did list. The result is no Specialized High School offer at all. Omitting a school is not strategy. It is a missed opportunity.


Reddit discussions also show that commute, school culture, and workload should factor into ranking decisions. One user emphasized that a shorter commute can meaningfully improve high school life, while others compared the day-to-day culture at Stuyvesant versus Bronx Science. Cutoff prestige is the wrong reason to rank a school.


## What SHSAT Score Should You Aim For?


There is no single SHSAT score that guarantees admission to every Specialized High School. A useful target depends on the school a student wants to attend, the student's current performance, and how much progress they can make before test day.


Use the latest published cutoffs as reference points, then build a preparation target above the historical result where practical. A higher target creates a buffer against year-to-year variation, but no fixed margin guarantees an offer.

### Is a 600 SHSAT score good?


A composite score of 600 is above every ninth-grade cutoff in the article's 2020–2026 historical comparison, including the reported Stuyvesant high of 566 in 2020. It is therefore a useful historical benchmark for ambitious preparation.


However, a score of 600 does not guarantee admission in a future year. Cutoffs are not fixed in advance, and students should use the most recent official guidance and their own practice results to assess readiness.


### How to turn a target into a study plan


Start by identifying the gap between current practice performance and the target you have chosen. Then break preparation into specific skills, such as reading comprehension, grammar, algebra, geometry, and problem-solving.


Review progress regularly and adjust the plan according to recurring errors. A diagnostic test and a structured study plan can help students focus their time on the skills most likely to benefit from additional practice.


## 10th-Grade SHSAT Cutoff Scores: Entry to Specialized High Schools


Students entering ninth grade for the first time may take the SHSAT for available 10th-grade seats at the testing Specialized High Schools. These results should be considered separately from the regular ninth-grade admissions cutoffs.


For 2026 admissions, the published 10th-grade cutoff figures include several scores that differ sharply from the ninth-grade results. The figures for Bronx Science and Brooklyn Latin are especially unusual and should be read with the accompanying source and methodology notes.


### Why are some 10th-grade cutoffs much higher?


The number of seats available for 10th-grade entry is limited and can vary by school and year. When relatively few offers are made, the lowest score receiving an offer can vary substantially between admissions cycles.

### How should students use 10th-grade cutoff data?


Students seeking 10th-grade entry should use the relevant 10th-grade results rather than the ninth-grade cutoff table. Review the latest official admissions guidance, confirm eligibility, and understand that a small number of available seats can make historical results less stable.


A previous cutoff is a reference point, not a promise that the same score will receive an offer in another year.


## How the Computer-Adaptive SHSAT Changes Preparation


Beginning fall 2026, the SHSAT is a computer-adaptive test. This is the biggest format change in the exam’s recent history, and many prep resources have not caught up.


The new format includes 50 ELA questions and 50 Math questions (replacing the old 114-question paper test), 180 minutes of standard test time, adaptive item selection that adjusts question difficulty based on performance, and limited ability to go back after moving forward on Math and stand-alone ELA questions. NYC Public Schools confirms these details on its[official testing page](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/learning/testing/specialized-high-school-admissions-test) .


That last restriction is the most disruptive change. The old strategy of skipping hard questions and returning later no longer works for most of the test. Passage-based ELA questions can be revisited within that passage set before submitting, but Math questions and stand-alone ELA questions are forward-only.


A practitioner commentary on LinkedIn from School of Math New York frames this as requiring a fundamental shift in pacing strategy, recommending that mock tests mirror the digital, no-skip-back format. Families preparing with old paper-test materials are practicing for an exam that no longer exists.


One community insight from Reddit’s TestingMomParents forum is worth sharing: harder questions on an adaptive test may actually be a good sign. Correct answers lead to harder questions, which means the test is finding the student’s upper range. Students should practice staying calm when difficulty rises rather than assuming they are failing.


Historical SHSAT cutoff scores remain useful for broad targeting, but old raw-score calculators tied to 114 questions are now unreliable. For families also planning ahead for the[SAT or ACT](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/sat-vs-act-key-differences-how-to-choose) , the computer-adaptive format will feel somewhat familiar, since the digital SAT also uses adaptive modules.

## Discovery Program and Cutoffs


The Discovery Program is not a second-chance waitlist for everyone who misses a cutoff. It is an invitation-only summer program for certain disadvantaged students who scored within a defined band below the cutoff.


For Summer 2026,[NYC Public Schools stated](https://www.schools.nyc.gov/enrollment/enroll-grade-by-grade/specialized-high-schools/discovery-programs) that any student scoring 495 or above was not eligible for Discovery. Participation required meeting specific eligibility criteria, receiving an invitation, and having listed the relevant school on the SHSAT registration.


That last requirement creates another version of the gap-zone problem. A student who scores just below a school’s cutoff but never listed that school cannot be considered for Discovery there. The school must appear on the student’s original ranked list. On Reddit, a detailed explainer about Discovery highlighted how families often assume “below cutoff” automatically means Discovery eligibility. It does not. The criteria are narrower than most people expect.


## Common Myths About SHSAT Cutoff Scores


**Myth: The cutoff is set before the test.**
Cutoffs are created after students are processed and seats are filled. No one knows the cutoff until offers go out.


**Myth: Ranking a lower-cutoff school first improves your chance.**
The matching system checks your ranked list in order. Ranking a “safer” school first means you receive that school’s offer even if your score would have cleared a higher-ranked school. It does not improve your odds.


**Myth: Scoring above last year’s cutoff guarantees admission this year.**
There is no guaranteed SHSAT score for any future year. Cutoffs can rise or fall depending on the applicant pool, preferences, and score distribution.


**Myth: Higher cutoff always means better school.**
Cutoffs reflect demand relative to seat count. Brooklyn Tech’s cutoff (506) is lower than HSMSE’s (539), but Brooklyn Tech makes roughly ten times more offers. Cutoff does not equal quality.


**Myth: The SHSAT is still 114 questions on paper.**
As of fall 2026, the test has 100 questions, is computer-adaptive, and uses different pacing rules.


**Myth: The SHSAT and LaGuardia admissions work the same way.**
LaGuardia is a Specialized High School but uses auditions, not the SHSAT. The SHSAT applies only to the eight testing schools.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What was the Stuyvesant cutoff score in 2026?


The Stuyvesant SHSAT cutoff score for Fall 2026 admissions (9th-grade entry) was 561. This was the highest cutoff among all eight testing Specialized High Schools.


### What was the Bronx Science cutoff score in 2026?


Bronx Science’s cutoff for Fall 2026 admissions was 525 for 9th-grade entry.


### What was the Brooklyn Tech cutoff score in 2026?


Brooklyn Tech’s cutoff for Fall 2026 admissions was 506 for 9th-grade entry. Despite being lower than several other schools, Brooklyn Tech made more offers (1,393) than any other testing Specialized High School.


### Is there a passing score for the SHSAT?


No. There is no single passing score. Each school has its own cutoff created after seats are filled. The SHSAT is scored on a composite scale, and each school’s cutoff depends on demand, score distribution, preference lists, and seat availability.


### When will the 2027 SHSAT cutoff scores be released?


Fall 2027 high school offers are scheduled for March 3, 2027. The 2027 cutoffs will be known after those offers go out. They cannot be predicted in advance.


### Can I get into a Specialized High School I did not rank?


No. Students are only matched to schools on their ranked preference list. If a school is not on the list, the student cannot receive an offer there, regardless of their score.


### Should I rank schools by cutoff difficulty instead of preference?


No. Rank schools in the order you would actually want to attend them. Ranking a lower-cutoff school first does not improve your odds of admission. It only prevents you from being matched to a school you preferred more.


### How is the fall 2026 SHSAT different from previous years?


The fall 2026 SHSAT is computer-adaptive with 50 ELA questions and 50 Math questions, 180 minutes of standard time, and limited ability to go back after advancing. This replaces the old 114-question paper format.
